clue.text: After a difficult term, is Diana recalled?

definitions.note: the Roman huntress calls to mind her Greek original

indicators.note: a difficult version of the letters is a troublesome jumble of them, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, mixed with the A before it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a princess is being called back after a hard spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' gives ARTEM, the anagram of A TERM. 'recalled' is part of the definition: Diana, the Roman huntress, calls to mind the Greek goddess she was modelled on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman goddess Diana was identified with the Greek huntress-goddess of the moon, so Diana evokes her Greek counterpart.

clue.text: The lack of faith in his team is disastrous

indicators.note: a disastrous state of the letters means they are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A coach laments that his side's lack of belief is calamitous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is disastrous' rearranges the letters of HIS TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheism is disbelief in any god, an absence of religious belief.

clue.text: Use machine to remove water that's fallen on railway

parts.note: tumbled means fell

explanation.surface: Rain has come down on the tracks and needs a machine to clear it.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundry is dried by turning it in a heated rotating drum.

clue.text: Lassie with little time to fool about

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time
to rag is to tease or fool around

explanation.surface: A young girl has a short while to play around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lassie' suggests the film dog, but it means a girl: this is a Scottish girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish girl's name is fittingly clued by the Scots word for a young girl.

clue.text: Part of horse's tackle appears to bend under burden

indicators.note: in a down answer, under means placed below the burden

parts.note: to saddle someone is to burden them
to bow is to bend

explanation.surface: A piece of riding gear seems to buckle under a heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: The arched front part of a saddle is a component of a horse's riding gear.

clue.text: Sort of rabbit to shoot? You'd be very lucky to hit it

definitions.text: You'd be very lucky to hit it

parts.note: a jack rabbit is a kind of hare-like rabbit
to pot is to shoot game

explanation.surface: A hunter after a particular rabbit is told that hitting it would take great luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitting the top prize in a lottery or fruit machine needs extraordinary luck.

clue.text: Extremely happy warrior

definitions.meaning: British informal for very, as in very good

explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: British slang for very, a word for cheerful, and a nickname for a Royal Marine soldier.

clue.text: Worthless stuff in chapter gets the bird

parts.note: chaff is husks, so anything worthless
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rubbish in a chapter of a book earns the author a raspberry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' suggests being booed, but 'the bird' is the definition: a common finch.
explanation.definitionFit: A common European finch with a pink breast is a small songbird.

clue.text: Charterhouse's deputy head was a poet

definitions.meaning: a monastery's second in command, below the abbot

explanation.definitionFit: A monk ranking next below an abbot, and Matthew Prior, the eighteenth-century English verse writer.

clue.text: Attempt to embrace girl in workplace

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within the arms, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: a try is an attempt
Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man tries to hug a girl at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A tannery is a factory where hides are processed into leather.

clue.text: In so far as it's possible, right for poet

parts.words: In so far as it's possible
parts.note: driving a nail home means driving it as far as it will go

explanation.surface: A vague hedge about doing what is possible, then a call for the right poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek epic writer of the Iliad and Odyssey is the archetypal poet.

clue.text: Spotted creature, weird animal at Land's End

indicators.note: the end of the word Land's is its final letter
weird suggests something oddly arranged, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A strange spotted animal is sighted at the far tip of Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: D from 'Land's End' comes first, then 'weird' rearranges ANIMAL AT into ALMATIAN. LAND'S END is the westernmost point of Cornwall in England.
explanation.definitionFit: This breed of dog is famous for its white coat covered with black spots.

clue.text: Against the rules, I left cricket side with partner

parts.note: the leg side is one half of a cricket field, the batter's legs side
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to quitting a cricket team with a friend, breaking the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the LEG side (also called on side).
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something unlawfully or contrary to regulations is the same as acting against the rules.

clue.text: Musical direction in place of note

parts.note: for can mean instead of, as in a substitute for
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A conductor's marking stands in for a written note.
explanation.definitionFit: A score marking telling players to play loudly is an instruction in music.

clue.text: He was given a golden rule

definitions.text: He was given a golden rule

parts.words: He was given a golden rule
parts.note: a moral precept sounds intended, but it is the mythical king granted a touch that turned all to gold, whose reign became golden

explanation.definitionFit: The Phrygian king of myth was granted a wish that everything he touched would become gold.

clue.text: Time of her youth, as sad lady recollected

indicators.note: re-collected means gathered again into a new order

explanation.surface: A melancholy woman remembers her girlhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' looks like remembering but splits as re-collected, the anagram signal for AS SAD LADY.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra calls her inexperienced past 'my salad days', a phrase for the green years of early life.

clue.text: Study of plants and tree found on Australian coast

parts.note: botany is the science of plants
the bay is a laurel tree

explanation.surface: A naturalist studies plants and a tree on an Australian shoreline.
explanation.definitionFit: The inlet near Sydney where Captain Cook landed lies on the eastern seaboard of Australia.

clue.text: Dismiss Jack's change of attitude

indicators.note: the 's of Jack's reads as has, so the dismissal phrase has the sailor held within it

parts.note: to turn out is to eject or dismiss
an able seaman, a jack tar, is abbreviated AB

explanation.surface: Sacking a sailor amounts to a reversal of policy.
explanation.walkthrough: To dismiss is to turn out, and like many English phrasal verbs it splits round its object: you turn someone out, so the sailor sits in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnabout is a complete reversal of opinion or policy.

clue.text: Present given by Ruth, say, to boy

parts.note: Ruth is a book of the Old Testament
taken as written
Ken is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A woman named Ruth gives a gift to a lad.
explanation.definitionFit: A voucher exchangeable at a bookshop is a gift.

clue.text: Vessel is liable to go down with 12 on board

indicators.note: on board means carried inside, so one piece sits within the others

parts.note: may expresses possibility, what is liable to happen
to lower is to go down or descend
the answer to 12 across is a musical marking abbreviated f

explanation.surface: A ship is at risk of sinking with a dozen people aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' is a cross-reference to the 12-across answer, the musical marking for loud, written as a single f in a score. That is the letter carried 'on board'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ship that carried the Pilgrim Fathers to America in 1620 is a famous sailing vessel.

clue.text: Exploit so soft a weakling

parts.note: to milk is to exploit
taken as written
p, piano, is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: Taking advantage of someone so gentle as a feeble person.
explanation.definitionFit: A milksop is a timid, ineffectual man, a feeble person.

clue.text: Scot's expression shows derision

definitions.meaning: a Scottish exclamation of impatience or dismissal
to jeer at someone with mocking calls

explanation.definitionFit: A Scots interjection of protest, and the verb for jeering or catcalling in mockery.

clue.text: It's a pity girl's lacking a date

parts.note: it's a sin is an idiom for it's a shame
Edie is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Sympathy for a girl who has no one to go out with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking a date' suggests a romantic partner, but it is the Latin legal phrase for an adjournment with no day fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin legal term describes an adjournment with no fixed day for resuming.

clue.text: Furious as a bowler, perhaps, about four or six

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is placed round the other

parts.note: a bowler hat is an example of a lid, slang for a hat
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone is as angry as a cricket bowler who has been hit for a boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests cricket, where four and six are boundary hits, but here it is the hat, slang 'lid'. Four or six both work, because six (VI) is four (IV) read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Livid is a strong word for enraged or very angry.

clue.text: Way in which head's left the meeting-place

indicators.note: the head of the word has left, so its first letter is dropped

parts.note: an avenue is a way or road

explanation.surface: A road on which the boss has walked out of the meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue is the place where an event or gathering is held.

clue.text: Fraud with article to flog that is stolen from fool initially

indicators.note: stolen from means taken away out of the word that follows

parts.note: a charlie is British slang for a fool
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is
a is the indefinite article
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: A conman with something to sell makes off with a simpleton's belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: IE leaves CHARLIE to give CHARL, which comes first ('initially'), then A and TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlatan is a quack or impostor, someone who pretends to skill he lacks.

clue.text: Primate wants church to overcome the devil

indicators.note: in a down answer, to overcome is to sit on top of, so the first piece goes above

parts.note: an imp is a little devil

explanation.surface: An archbishop needs the church to defeat Satan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop, which the church setting supports, but it is the ape.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimpanzee is an ape, a member of the primate order.

clue.text: Misanthrope I found side-splitting

indicators.note: splitting means breaking apart, so one piece goes between the letters of another

parts.note: L and R, the left and right sides
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone who hates people found something hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side-splitting' reads as hilarious, but ONE (I) splits the two sides, L and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A loner avoids company, as someone who dislikes people would.

clue.text: Small country resort for Romanians

indicators.note: to resort is to sort again, putting the letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A holiday destination is suggested for visitors from Romania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but is the anagram signal: re-sort the letters of ROMANIANS.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny republic surrounded by Italy is one of the smallest states in Europe.

clue.text: Defenceless king protected by churchman in retreat

indicators.note: protected by means held inside the following piece
a retreat goes backwards, so the churchman's title is read in reverse

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: A vulnerable monarch is sheltered by a cleric on a religious retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns DEAN into NAED, and K goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without clothing or cover leaves one exposed and unprotected.

clue.text: It contains a rising by force of arms

definitions.text: It contains a rising by force of arms

parts.words: It contains a rising by force of arms
parts.note: an armed rebellion seems meant, but it is a gym exercise in which the body is raised by pushing with the arms

explanation.definitionFit: This floor exercise lifts the body by straightening the arms, so each repetition is an arm-powered lift.

clue.text: Playwright's sweetheart featured in centre spread

indicators.note: featured in means appearing within, so one piece sits inside another
spread out suggests the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: A dramatist's girlfriend appears in a magazine's middle pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges CENTRE into TERNCE; E, the heart of 'sweet', goes inside it. The 's of 'Playwright's' is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman comic dramatist Publius Terentius Afer wrote six surviving plays.
